notes: The word 'Trinity' is not in the Bible. These are the verses on God's oneness and on Father, Son and Spirit together.
These are among the hardest passages in the Bible. Some of the Fathers read them as a picture of the spiritual battle, and others admit them to be a difficulty.

These texts belong to the law of ancient Israel. Some limit slavery (release after six years, a runaway slave not to be returned). Some allow it, including of foreigners. Readers still argue about what they mean for us.

The Sermon on the Mount speaks of turning the other cheek. Romans 13 gives the ruler the sword. Israel's wars of conquest are in Joshua and Deuteronomy. The tradition holds these together in different ways.
The law forbids interest on loans to a poor fellow Israelite, and allows it with foreigners. The Fathers and councils applied this to Christians.
